Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the team and get a sense of your production flows. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key items and next steps so we stay aligned on the RTBF/deletion requirements you flagged.

Summary of ask:
- Customer data deletion (RTBF) initiated via API or portal by FintechCo
- Required purge timeline: primary stores within 72 hours, backups within 30 days where feasible
- Proof of deletion: audit log entries and a timestamped export for legal
- Data residency: US-only processing for the initial pilot
- Logging/PII: redact PII in logs after X days; retain non-PII debug traces for 90 days

What I committed to check/confirm internally:
1) Exact timelines for backup retention and physical deletion from snapshot lifecycle (we need to confirm constraints for third-party backup providers)
2) The format and fields we can include in a deletion audit (we can provide per-request audit entries including request id, user, timestamp, and model/version)
3) Whether we can support an API-triggered purge for your pilot + a documented manual escalation path for DSRs

Next steps / owners:
- Camila (me): validate backup purge feasibility and provide a proposed timeline + exceptions matrix by EOD Wed (Mar 18)
- Monica (cc): loop in Customer Success to capture any operational concerns during deletions
- Ben / FintechCo: share the legal/DSR PDF you mentioned during the call (if possible) so we can map fields

Attachments: Please attach your RTBF template if you have one — that will speed verification.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short note once I have the backup clarity.

Thanks Camila — that recap is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Primary goal: for pilot customers we need deletions to be irreversible from the platform within 7 days for primary stores, and we understand backups may require a longer window; we'd like a max of 45 days for backup purges where vendor-process constraints exist.
- Compliance requires a signed attestation that deletion requests were executed; a CSV of request ids + timestamps is sufficient.
- We cannot accept any long-term retention of PII in logs beyond 30 days; any logging that may include PII must be redacted at that point.
- For data residency, the pilot will be US-only but we will evaluate EU later — please note this for any routing/fallback policies.

Attached is our RTBF request template and the legal checklist. Can you confirm whether your team has any known limitations around backup snapshot deletion or immutable backups?

Hi Alice — thanks for the fast reply and for sending the template. Looping in Monica (CS) and Aditya (Solutions) to validate operational/infra details — summary below.

Short answers (we'll follow up with a doc):
- Primary store deletion: we can signal deletion to the serving layer and remove customer-specific data within 72 hours in most cases; we will commit to confirm 7-day irreversible behavior for the pilot customers (engineering caveats noted below).
- Backup snapshots: many cloud storage providers retain snapshots beyond immediate deletion due to snapshot chains, replication windows, and provider SLAs. Typical achievable window without special provider contracts is 30–45 days; we will propose 30 days as standard and flag 45 days maximum for legacy backups. If FintechCo requires contract-level guarantees for 14 days, we can discuss a dedicated retention policy under Dedicated/Private deployment.
- Audit proof: we can provide a CSV export with request id, initiating user, timestamp, model/version, and deletion status. We will include a signed attestation option via DocuSign for enterprise contracts.
- Logging/PII: our standard practice is to tokenize/redact PII in logs after 30 days; we can accelerate to 14 days for high-risk fields on a per-account basis if required.

Engineering caveats to confirm (Aditya / Monica):
- Are there any objects stored outside our control plane (partner-managed backups) that would require additional vendor coordination?
- Can we instrument a purge job that marks backup snapshots for expedited GC, and what are the implications for cross-region replication?

Action items and owners:
- Aditya: confirm snapshot GC feasibility and whether we can guarantee a 30-day backup purge for the pilot (due COB Wed 18 Mar).
- Monica: prepare a short runbook for FintechCo's team on how to initiate RTBF via API + manual support path.
- Camila: collate these answers and share a draft attestation + CSV format.

Thanks — will be back shortly with the internal answers.

Best,
Camila

Hi all — quick engineering update after reviewing infra constraints.

- Primary stores: we can implement a deletion marker that triggers immediate removal of customer-indexed data; fully irreversible garbage collection runs in our pipeline and will complete within 24–72 hours depending on queued GC cycles. That matches Camila's note.
- Backups / snapshots: for the hosted setup, snapshots are managed by our cloud provider and typically retained for 30 days. We do not currently have the ability to retroactively force-delete provider-level immutable snapshots without a commercial SLA. For customers requiring stricter guarantees (e.g., 7–14 day total footprint), we advise Dedicated or Private deployment where we can adjust snapshot lifecycle and retention via account-level policies.
- Audit exports: we can generate a CSV for each deletion request with the fields you requested. We can also provide a signed attestation from legal for enterprise contracts.

Proposed pilot commitments:
- Primary deletion: remove customer data from live serving within 72 hours, GC irreversible within 7 days for typical cases; we will provide CSV attestations for each request.
- Backup purge: standard 30-day retention; up to 45 days where provider snapshot chains exist.
- Logs: default PII redaction at 30 days; can be shortened to 14 days on request for the pilot (requires flagging during onboarding).

If FintechCo is comfortable with the proposed pilot commitments, we can draft the attestation and runbook for signature and onboarding.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
